when.quote: Use this process when a customer believes there is a discrepancy between the cash back they received for a particular transaction and the cash back they should have received.

info.about: The customer's full name, email or user id, used to look up their record
info.ask: Could you please give me your full name so I can look up your account?

info.about: Any 2 of: date of birth, email, phone number, address. They must match the record.
info.ask: To verify your identity, could you give me two of the following: your date of birth, email, phone number or home address?

info.about: The customer's credit card accounts: card type, account id and opening date (the opening date matters for promotions)
Each credit card transaction: transaction_id, card type, merchant, amount, category, date and rewards_earned in points
Any purchases the customer already suspects. This is optional. If the customer does not know, the agent checks every transaction.
info.ask: Are there particular purchases you are concerned about, or would you like me to review all of your credit card transactions?

steps.do: Greet the customer. Ask for the customer identifier and two verification values.
steps.quote: To verify the identity of the user, call the appropriate read tools, and ensure that they are able to give correctly any 2 out of the following values: date of birth, email, phone number, address.

args.customer_name: the name the customer gave (case sensitive); use get_user_information_by_email or get_user_information_by_id instead if the customer gave one of those

steps.quote: To verify the identity of the user, call the appropriate read tools

steps.do: Check that at least 2 of the values the customer gave match the record. If they do not match, do not continue and do not reveal any account data.
steps.quote: Knowing full name or userID is not enough to verify.

steps.do: Get the current timestamp for the verification log
steps.quote: If you need the current time, always use the get_current_time() tool.
After verification, you must call the verification logging tool to properly log the information into the verification records.

steps.do: Get the customer's credit card accounts: card types and opening dates
steps.quote: Recalculate the correct rewards for each transaction based on the card type, transaction category, and any applicable promotions.

steps.do: Get all of the customer's credit card transactions
steps.quote: When you contact us, we'll look into the specific transaction, verify the merchant category, check the applicable reward rates for your card, and determine if an adjustment is needed.

steps.do: For every transaction, work out the correct points. Use the card's rate for the category, then apply merchant exclusions and any active promotion. Points = floor(amount × rate% × 100) for cash back cards, or floor(amount × points per dollar) for EcoCard. Compare the result with rewards_earned. Label each transaction correct, underpaid or overpaid.
steps.quote: Ensure your calculation reflects the proper base rate and any active bonus category or promotion at the time of purchase.

steps.do: Tell the customer which transactions do not match, giving the merchant, amount, points received and correct points. Tell them how many points each one is short.
steps.quote: If we find that you were indeed shortchanged on your rewards, we'll make sure the correct amount is applied to your account.

steps.do: Give the customer the cash back dispute tool
steps.if: at least one transaction is underpaid (or has another discrepancy the agent decides to dispute; see open questions)
steps.quote: Tool to provide to the user: `submit_cash_back_dispute_0589(user_id: str, transaction_id: str)`

steps.do: Tell the customer exactly what to enter: their user_id and each transaction_id to dispute, one submission per transaction. Confirm the ids are correct. Say that supporting context may be requested later.
steps.quote: Confirm the customer has the correct transaction_id before they submit.

steps.do: Submit one dispute for each transaction
steps.quote: Tell the customer to run the tool with their own user_id and the specific transaction_id for the purchase in question.

steps.do: Unlock the tool that updates a transaction's rewards
steps.if: the dispute(s) come back resolved and approved
steps.quote: Use `unlock_discoverable_agent_tool` to unlock the agent tool `update_transaction_rewards_3847`.

steps.do: Set the corrected rewards on each approved transaction

arguments.new_rewards_earned: 'X points', where X is the recalculated whole-number value (never the expected_rewards from the dispute record)

steps.quote: new_rewards_earned: a string formatted as 'X points' where X is the correct whole-number point value

steps.do: Re-read the transactions to confirm the updated rewards
steps.quote: Confirm the update in credit_card_transaction_history after the tool call completes.

steps.do: Summarise the corrected transactions and new point values for the customer. Tell them 1 point = $0.01 in cash back.
steps.quote: For example, 250 points equals $2.50 in cash back, which matches a 2.5% cash back rate on a $100 purchase.

rules.rule: Recalculate the correct rewards yourself. Never use the expected_rewards field in a dispute record.
rules.quote: Important: Do not rely on any expected_rewards field in the dispute record. Independently verify rates and eligibility.

rules.rule: Points are always floored to a whole number. For cash back cards, points = floor(amount × rate% × 100), for example $99.99 at 2.5% = 249 points.
rules.quote: All credit card rewards points are rounded down to the nearest whole number.

rules.rule: Rewards are stored as points: 1 point = $0.01 for cash back cards
rules.quote: For example, 250 points equals $2.50 in cash back, which matches a 2.5% cash back rate on a $100 purchase.

rules.rule: Apply a correction only after the dispute is resolved and approved
rules.quote: After a cash back dispute is resolved and approved, you must update the affected transaction(s) with the correct rewards value.

rules.rule: The customer submits the dispute with the user tool. The agent does not submit it.
rules.quote: Tell the customer to run the tool with their own user_id and the specific transaction_id for the purchase in question.

jobs.done_when: Every transaction has been recalculated. A dispute has been submitted by the customer for each transaction chosen for correction. Each approved dispute's transaction has been updated with update_transaction_rewards_3847 to the recalculated 'X points' and confirmed in the transaction history. The customer has been told the outcome.

documents.why: Internal cash back dispute procedure. It names the user tool submit_cash_back_dispute_0589.
Internal procedure for applying corrections with update_transaction_rewards_3847 after approval. It requires independent recalculation.
Rewards are stored as points: 1 point = $0.01 cash back. EcoCard earns points per dollar.
Customer-facing description of investigating cash back discrepancies
Business Silver double cash back promotion
Silver Zoom triple cash back promotion

open_questions: Overpaid transactions: doc 003 covers any 'discrepancy', which suggests both directions. Every customer-facing text (doc 021) speaks only of being shortchanged, and no document says to reduce rewards that were overpaid. The default here is to dispute and correct only underpaid transactions. If the customer asks for an overpayment to be corrected, the documents neither require nor forbid it. This needs a policy decision.
The agent has no tool to read the cash_back_disputes database. The approved/resolved status must come from the result of submit_cash_back_dispute_0589.
Whether the customer actually claimed the Silver Zoom triple cash back promotion cannot be seen in the records the agent has.

The customer may say they cannot use tools. The KB still says the customer runs submit_cash_back_dispute_0589 with the user tool. The agent should give the tool and walk the customer through it with the exact argument values.
Identity verification rests on the system policy, not a KB document, so those steps cite 'policy'.
